title: The Most Expensive Pickups You Can Buy in 2026 (One Costs $122,265)

scenes.text: In nineteen twenty-five, Ford's first factory pickup cost two hundred eighty-one dollars. In twenty twenty-six, a fully loaded Ford pickup can cost one hundred twenty-two thousand. The average full-size pickup in America now sells for more than sixty-seven thousand dollars. And at least nine pickups on sale right now cost more than ninety thousand. Here are the most expensive pickups you can buy, and the twist about who is actually buying them.
scenes.caption: $281 IN 1925. $122,265 IN 2026

scenes.text: This is not just a story about rich buyers. Rising prices at the top pull up prices for everyone. When top trims sell well, carmakers build more of them and fewer basic trucks, and the average price climbs. That is one reason the cheapest full-size trucks are harder to find at dealers today. What happens at the top of the market affects your price too.
scenes.caption: THE TOP PULLS EVERYONE UP

scenes.text: We ranked them by real numbers. Fully loaded prices for the half-ton trucks, and starting prices for the electric super trucks. We will show you where the money goes, which options add tens of thousands of dollars, and why one of these trucks has a rooftop tent on the options list. And at the end, the checklist that keeps you from overpaying for any truck, at any price.
scenes.caption: WHERE THE MONEY GOES

scenes.text: Every number in this video comes from a published source, listed in the description. Prices change often, so always check the current price before you buy. If we could not confirm a figure, we left it out. First, a reality check on what normal trucks cost in twenty twenty-six.
scenes.caption: EVERY NUMBER IS SOURCED

scenes.text: According to Kelley Blue Book data from Cox Automotive, the average transaction price for a full-size pickup in September twenty twenty-six was sixty-seven thousand, five hundred seventy-three dollars, up one point five percent from a year earlier. The average for all new vehicles was fifty thousand, five hundred sixty-two. So a normal full-size truck costs about seventeen thousand dollars more than the average new vehicle.
scenes.caption: FULL-SIZE PICKUP AVG: $67,573
scenes.chapter: What a normal truck costs in 2026

scenes.text: And the brands are not equal. In the same report, Ram had the highest average transaction price of the major truck brands, at sixty-eight thousand, three hundred fifty-one dollars, up four point six percent. GMC averaged sixty-five thousand, five hundred thirty-two. Ford averaged fifty-nine thousand, nine hundred sixty-three, and Chevrolet forty-nine thousand, four hundred sixty-five. Those are brand averages across every vehicle they sell, not just trucks.
scenes.caption: RAM BRAND AVG: $68,351

scenes.text: Why are trucks so expensive? Part of it is what buyers ask for. Crew cabs, four-wheel drive, big screens, leather, driver assistance systems and powerful engines all add cost. Part of it is inflation and tariffs on vehicles and parts. And part of it is simple business. Trucks are among the most profitable vehicles carmakers sell, and top trims are where the biggest profits are.
scenes.caption: WHY TRUCKS COST SO MUCH

scenes.text: Here is the twist. Back in two thousand two, Lincoln tried to sell a luxury pickup called the Blackwood for fifty-two thousand dollars, and it flopped. Buyers said it was too expensive. Today, the average full-size pickup costs much more than that. The luxury truck that failed in two thousand two is cheaper than a normal truck in twenty twenty-six, at least on paper, before inflation.
scenes.caption: TWIST: THE $52K FLOP

scenes.text: Now the list. We start with the five most expensive half-ton pickups, ranked by Pickup Truck Talk in January twenty twenty-six, with every option and the destination fee added. Number five is the Chevrolet Silverado fifteen hundred Z R two A E V Bison, at ninety-two thousand, six hundred three dollars fully loaded.
scenes.caption: 5. SILVERADO ZR2 BISON: $92,603

scenes.text: The Z R two is Chevy's serious off-road truck, and the Bison package, built with the off-road company A E V, adds armor, special bumpers and skid plates. The loaded truck uses the six point two liter V eight. Pickup Truck Talk added an eight hundred fifty dollar air intake and a one hundred ninety-five dollar active exhaust. According to CarGurus, the regular Silverado Z R two starts at seventy-four thousand five hundred ninety-five.
scenes.caption: ZR2 BASE: $74,595

scenes.text: The Bison is also a reminder of how much off-road capability now costs. Twenty years ago, an off-road package might add a few thousand dollars for skid plates and better shocks. Today, a full off-road truck with armor, special suspension and big tires sits near the top of the price list. Off-road is no longer an option. It is a luxury category of its own.
scenes.caption: OFF-ROAD IS A LUXURY NOW

scenes.text: And here is the twist. Pickup Truck Talk called it the most affordable half-ton for twenty twenty-six with all options added. Read that again. The cheapest truck on a list of the most expensive trucks still costs more than ninety-two thousand dollars. That tells you how high the ceiling has climbed.
scenes.caption: THE 'CHEAPEST' IS $92K

scenes.text: Number four is the Toyota Tundra Capstone, at ninety-eight thousand, four hundred forty-one dollars fully loaded. The Capstone is Toyota's luxury Tundra, with a hybrid powertrain. According to CarGurus, it starts at eighty-two thousand, nine hundred ninety-five dollars, and the i-Force Max hybrid makes four hundred thirty-seven horsepower and five hundred eighty-three pound-feet of torque.
scenes.caption: 4. TUNDRA CAPSTONE: $98,441

scenes.text: How does a Tundra get to almost one hundred thousand dollars? The options. According to Pickup Truck Talk, they included a two thousand five hundred dollar Dometic rooftop tent, a one thousand seven hundred nine dollar A R B fridge and freezer, and a nine hundred ninety dollar A R B portable compressor. Toyota offers so many accessories that the Tundra slipped past the Chevy.
scenes.caption: A $2,500 ROOFTOP TENT

scenes.text: This shows a new trend in expensive trucks: the overlanding lifestyle. Buyers want a truck that can take them into the wilderness and let them sleep there. Rooftop tents, fridges and air compressors used to be aftermarket products. Now some carmakers sell them right on the order sheet, and roll them into the truck loan.
scenes.caption: THE OVERLANDING BOOM

scenes.text: The twist is that the Tundra is not a big seller next to the Detroit trucks. According to autoevolution, it sold one hundred ten thousand and eighty units through September twenty twenty-six. But Toyota has found that the buyers it does have are willing to spend a lot. The brand's average transaction price, across all its vehicles, rose four point nine percent in September, the biggest increase of the major truck brands.
scenes.caption: TOYOTA ATP: +4.9%

scenes.text: Number three is the G M C Sierra fifteen hundred Denali Ultimate, at ninety-nine thousand, six hundred thirty-nine dollars fully loaded. According to Pickup Truck Talk, it starts at eighty-four thousand four hundred, and the author called it a luxurious dream. It has open-pore wood, premium leather and a huge screen. It is G M C's answer to the luxury car.
scenes.caption: 3. SIERRA DENALI ULTIMATE: $99,639

scenes.text: The options say a lot about this buyer. Pickup Truck Talk added a one thousand ninety-five dollar Glacier White Tricoat paint and a three thousand eight hundred ninety-five dollar Brembo brake upgrade. And according to CarGurus, the Denali Ultimate can be ordered with a three liter Duramax diesel inline six, with three hundred five horsepower and four hundred ninety-five pound-feet of torque.
scenes.caption: $3,895 BRAKES, $1,095 PAINT

scenes.text: The Denali Ultimate is aimed at a buyer who might otherwise buy a luxury S U V. It offers the same kind of interior quality, with the added ability to tow and haul. For many families, it is a single vehicle that replaces two. That is the argument G M C makes, and it is why the brand can charge so much.
scenes.caption: ONE VEHICLE REPLACES TWO

scenes.text: Here is the twist. The Sierra is built on the same basic platform as the Chevrolet Silverado. So G M C is selling the same engineering for much more money, by changing the brand, the interior and the image. And it works. In September twenty twenty-six, G M C's average transaction price was sixty-five thousand, five hundred thirty-two dollars, far above Chevrolet's forty-nine thousand, four hundred sixty-five.
scenes.caption: SAME PLATFORM, $16K MORE (AVG)

scenes.text: Number two is the Ram fifteen hundred R H O, at one hundred thousand, four hundred fifty-nine dollars fully loaded. It is the first truck on the list to break one hundred thousand. According to Pickup Truck Talk, the R H O starts just north of seventy-three thousand dollars, and the author added a nine thousand nine hundred ninety-five dollar R H O Level One Equipment Group.
scenes.caption: 2. RAM 1500 RHO: $100,459

scenes.text: The R H O is Ram's high-performance off-road truck, powered by the high output version of the three liter Hurricane inline six. According to CarGurus, that engine makes five hundred forty horsepower and five hundred twenty-one pound-feet of torque. It replaced the supercharged T R X for a year, as Ram's answer to the Ford Raptor.
scenes.caption: HURRICANE HO: 540 HP

scenes.text: And here is the twist. Ram is not stopping there. In January twenty twenty-six, according to Pickup Truck Talk, Ram announced the return of the T R X for the twenty twenty-seven model year, with a supercharged six point two liter V eight, seven hundred seventy-seven horsepower, and a price just shy of one hundred thousand dollars before destination fees and likely dealer markups. Pickup Truck Talk noted that the T R X will obviously change this list for twenty twenty-seven.
scenes.caption: 2027 TRX: 777 HP, ~$100K

scenes.text: Think about what this means for the Ford Raptor. For years, Ford had the high-performance off-road truck market almost to itself. Now Ram has both the R H O and the returning T R X. The fight over the fastest, most extreme pickup is one of the most expensive arms races in the car business, and every new round pushes prices higher.
scenes.caption: THE $100K ARMS RACE

scenes.text: Ram also has the Tungsten, its most luxurious fifteen hundred. According to CarGurus, it starts at ninety-one thousand, five hundred ninety-five dollars. That makes Ram the brand with two different trucks starting around or above ninety thousand: one for luxury, one for speed. It also helps explain why Ram has the highest average transaction price of the big truck brands.
scenes.caption: RAM TUNGSTEN: $91,595 START

scenes.text: Number one among the half-tons is the Ford F-one-fifty Raptor R, at one hundred twenty-two thousand, two hundred sixty-five dollars fully loaded, according to Pickup Truck Talk. It has a five point two liter supercharged V eight with seven hundred twenty horsepower. It is a desert racing truck that you can buy at a Ford dealer.
scenes.caption: 1. F-150 RAPTOR R: $122,265

scenes.text: How much do the options add? According to Pickup Truck Talk, nearly forty thousand dollars. That is more than the price of many new cars, just in options. A buyer could buy a whole Ford Maverick for the cost of the extras on this one truck. According to The Truth About Cars, the Maverick currently starts at about thirty thousand dollars.
scenes.caption: OPTIONS: NEARLY $40,000

scenes.text: The Raptor R also shows how performance trucks hold their appeal. The original S V T Lightning from the nineties went from about twenty thousand dollars to forty-eight thousand seven hundred for good examples between twenty sixteen and twenty twenty-four, according to Ford Authority. Special, limited performance trucks can become collectibles. That does not happen to every expensive truck, but it does happen to some.
scenes.caption: SOME BECOME COLLECTIBLES

scenes.text: Here is the twist. The F-one-fifty is the best-selling truck line in America, with eight hundred twenty-eight thousand, eight hundred thirty-two F-Series sold in twenty twenty-five, according to Ford. The same nameplate covers trucks from the basic work truck to a one hundred twenty thousand dollar Raptor R. That range is one of the secrets of the F-Series. There is an F-one-fifty for almost every budget.
scenes.caption: ONE NAME, $40K TO $122K

scenes.text: Now the electric super trucks, because they push the price even higher. According to CarGurus in June twenty twenty-six, the G M C Hummer E V Pickup three X starts at one hundred seven thousand, nine hundred ninety-five dollars. It has three motors, one thousand horsepower, more than one thousand pound-feet of torque, and about three hundred fifty miles of range.
scenes.caption: HUMMER EV 3X: $107,995

scenes.text: The Chevrolet Silverado E V R S T Max Range is listed by CarGurus at one hundred eight thousand, four hundred forty-five dollars. The Tesla Cybertruck Cyberbeast is listed at one hundred eight thousand, seven hundred sixty, with zero to sixty in two point six seconds. And the most expensive of all is the Rivian R one T Quad, at one hundred fifteen thousand, nine hundred ninety dollars plus destination, with one thousand twenty-five horsepower.
scenes.caption: RIVIAN R1T QUAD: $115,990

scenes.text: And here is the biggest twist of the video. These are some of the most powerful pickups ever built, and they are struggling to sell. According to Cox Automotive estimates reported by InsideEVs, Cybertruck sales fell to about twenty thousand two hundred in twenty twenty-five. Ford ended the all-electric F-one-fifty Lightning after a nineteen point five billion dollar charge, according to Fox Business. The most expensive trucks are not always the ones buyers want.
scenes.caption: MOST POWERFUL, HARDEST TO SELL

scenes.text: The electric trucks are also the most powerful on the list by far. One thousand horsepower in the Hummer and more than one thousand in the Rivian. That is more than double many supercars from twenty years ago. But truck buyers do not buy on horsepower alone. They buy on towing range, charging, and price, and that is where the electric trucks lose ground.
scenes.caption: 1,000 HP ISN'T ENOUGH

scenes.text: Why? Price is part of it. When a truck costs more than one hundred thousand dollars, the buyer pool gets tiny. And the end of the federal electric vehicle tax credit in twenty twenty-five made the gap wider. A gas Raptor R or a Denali Ultimate sells to a buyer who already loves trucks. An electric super truck has to convince that buyer to change everything at once.
scenes.caption: WHY $100K EVs STRUGGLE

scenes.text: So who is buying ninety and one hundred thousand dollar pickups? For many, a top-trim truck replaces a luxury car. It carries the family, tows the boat, and has the leather and screens of a premium sedan. For business owners, a truck can also come with tax and business-use considerations, which is something to discuss with an accountant, not a salesperson.
scenes.caption: WHO BUYS $100K TRUCKS?
scenes.chapter: Who buys them and the real cost

scenes.text: And here is the twist on financing. Most buyers do not pay cash. A higher price means a bigger loan and more interest. A truck that looks affordable as a monthly payment can cost far more over a long loan. That is why the sticker price is only the beginning of the real cost of an expensive truck.
scenes.caption: THE PAYMENT TRAP

scenes.text: There is also depreciation. Expensive trucks often lose more dollars in value in their first years, simply because there are more dollars to lose. A one hundred thousand dollar truck that loses a third of its value has lost more than thirty thousand dollars. Some special models, like limited performance trucks, can hold value well. Many luxury trims do not.
scenes.caption: MORE DOLLARS TO LOSE

scenes.text: And remember the heavy-duty trucks. Fully loaded versions of the Ford Super Duty, the Ram heavy-duty and the Silverado and Sierra heavy-duty trucks, with diesel engines and top trims, can also climb into six figures. For buyers who tow very heavy trailers, those trucks are tools, not toys, and the price reflects the engineering needed to pull that weight.
scenes.caption: HEAVY-DUTY: ALSO SIX FIGURES

scenes.text: So what is the pattern? The most expensive pickups fall into three groups. Luxury trucks, like the Denali Ultimate, the Tungsten and the Capstone. Performance off-road trucks, like the Raptor R, the R H O and the Z R two Bison. And electric super trucks, like the Hummer E V, the Cybertruck and the Rivian. Each group is chasing a different buyer.
scenes.caption: 3 KINDS OF $100K TRUCKS

scenes.text: And the final twist. The truck that made pickups popular, the Model T runabout, cost two hundred eighty-one dollars in nineteen twenty-five, according to The Henry Ford. It was built to be affordable for anyone who worked. One hundred years later, the most expensive pickups cost more than many houses did a few decades ago. The pickup went from the cheapest vehicle you could buy to one of the most expensive.
scenes.caption: FROM CHEAPEST TO PRICIEST

scenes.text: So how do you avoid overpaying, at any price? First, compare the average transaction price, not the sticker. If full-size trucks average about sixty-seven thousand dollars, know where your truck sits against that. Second, look at what each option really costs. On a fully loaded truck, options can add tens of thousands of dollars that you may never use.
scenes.caption: CHECKS 1 AND 2: AVERAGE, OPTIONS
scenes.chapter: What to check before you buy in 2027

scenes.text: A good test is to price the truck two ways. First, the exact truck you want, fully loaded. Then the same truck with only the options you will really use every week. The difference is often ten or twenty thousand dollars. Ask yourself whether those extras are worth that money over the years you will own the truck, including the interest on the loan.
scenes.caption: PRICE IT TWO WAYS

scenes.text: Third, watch for dealer markups on hot models, like the new T R X. Fourth, compare the same engineering under different badges, like Silverado and Sierra. And fifth, count the full cost: loan interest, insurance, fuel and depreciation over five years. The real price of an expensive truck is much higher than the number on the window.
scenes.caption: CHECKS 3, 4 AND 5

scenes.text: We put all of these checks into the Twenty Twenty-Seven Truck Buyer's Guide, with the numbers to compare and the questions to ask every dealer. The link is in the description and in the pinned comment. Subscribe for the next video, where we go to the other end of the market: the cheapest new trucks in America. Thanks for watching.
